intro: Use me, te, le to mark the person affected or receiving a service.
p.cortarse el pelo: to have one's hair cut; to cut one's own hair
p.teñirse.nota: In the present, e changes to i: me tiño.
b1.titulo: Whose is it? The pronoun says so
b1.texto:
English often uses my, your, his. With body parts, clothes and belongings, Spanish commonly uses an indirect-object pronoun plus the article.

- **Le** robaron **el** coche. (They stole his car.)
- **Me** han manchado **la** camisa. (They stained my shirt.)
- **Te** duele **la** muela. (Your tooth hurts.)

For an accidental event, use **se + me/te/le**: **Se me ha roto** el móvil; **Se le ha perdido** la cartera. Plural forms include **se nos**, **se os** and **se les**.

**Me he cortado el pelo** often means “I got my hair cut,” but it can also mean “I cut my own hair”; context tells us which. **Me han cortado el pelo** makes clear that someone else did it. For other services, an indirect-object pronoun marks the person receiving the service: **Me han arreglado** el grifo; **me sacaron** una muela; **me revisaron** el coche. The person who did the work can be left unnamed.

An offer: **¿Te hago** un café? **¿Te llevo** la maleta?
b2.f0: What a change! Have you had your hair cut?
b2.f1: Yes, and I've had it dyed. I went to the hairdresser's this morning.
b2.f2: I've been at home with the plumber. One of our taps has broken.
b2.f3: Has he fixed it for you yet?
b2.f4: Yes. And my brother had his bike stolen last night.
b2.f5: What a day! Shall I make you a coffee?
b4.o0.refuerzo: Le shows whose car it was.
b4.o1.refuerzo: Spanish uses le and the article.
b4.o2.refuerzo: Lo would be the thing stolen.
b5.o0.refuerzo: It happened to me: se me.
b5.o1.refuerzo: The pronoun is me, with the article.
b6.pregunta: In «Me han cortado el pelo», who does me refer to?
b6.o0.refuerzo: Me marks the person affected; han indicates that someone else did the haircut.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The people doing it are the unstated subject of han cortado.
b6.o2.refuerzo: El pelo is the direct object; me is the affected person.
b7.pregunta: Complete: my shirt has been stained.
b7.o0.refuerzo: With me, Spanish uses the article.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Me already says whose shirt it is.
b8.pregunta: Translate: «Shall I make you a coffee?» (tú)
b9.traduccion: My brother had his bike stolen.
b10.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write about services you have had done lately and things that have been done to you: haircut, repairs, a theft.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Tell aloud about a time when something was stolen from you or broke.
